paper.title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency
paper.central_claim: LLM+P turns a natural-language planning problem into a PDDL problem file with a GPT-4 one-shot prompt, solves it with a classical planner (Fast Downward), and translates the plan back to natural language; LLM+P is able to provide optimal solutions for most problems while LLMs on their own fail to provide even feasible plans for most problems, and it is demonstrated on a real-robot tidy-up task.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope (B-leaning, offline evidence): LLM front end + classical planner as a robot task-planning harness; open-loop symbolic evaluation plus one real-robot demonstration.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method; 7 IPC domains x 20 tasks, GPT-4 temperature 0, one response; LLM+P optimal 64/140 (45.7%), feasible 97/140 (69.3%) vs direct GPT-4 ~17% correct; no-context LLM+P 0%; domain PDDL given only to LLM+P; single robot route-cost demo (22 vs 31). 'Optimal for most' unsupported. Expected offline, scoped; in scope via robot framing and R01 pattern.

signatures.object: Problem-file writer: GPT-4 translates a natural-language problem into a PDDL problem file given a human-written domain and one (description, problem PDDL) example.
signatures.information: Sees the natural-language problem and one worked example; the domain PDDL (predicates, action preconditions/effects) is supplied by a human expert to the planner and is task-agnostic; ground-truth problem PDDL is not shown.
signatures.operation: One-shot in-context translation at temperature 0; single attempt per task.
signatures.output: Problem PDDL file (objects, init, goal, optional metric).
signatures.conditions: Domain file and example exist for each domain; whether to invoke the pipeline is assumed known.
signatures.feedback: none (no planner-failure feedback to the LLM)
signatures.claimed_effect: With context LLM+P solves 90% Blocksworld, 95% Grippers, 85% Storage; without context 0% in all domains.
signatures.failure_boundary: Missing initial conditions (Floortile 0%), hard spatial domains (Termes 20%, Barman 20% optimal), translation errors undetected.

signatures.object: Delegated planning and read-out: Fast Downward solves the generated problem and the LLM re-expresses the plan in natural language.
signatures.information: Planner sees domain file and generated problem file; LLM sees the PDDL plan.
signatures.operation: Run seq-opt-fdss-1 (optimal) or lama (suboptimal) for up to 200 s; back-translate the resulting plan.
signatures.output: Optimal or feasible plan text; for the robot demo an 'optimal tidy-up plan' of cost 22.
signatures.conditions: Time limit 200 s; sound/complete planner returns a plan only if the problem file is consistent.
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable (optimal alias reported, lama as fallback in parentheses)
signatures.claimed_effect: Plans are optimal when the problem file is correct (soundness of the planner); demo cost 22 vs 31 for LLM-as-P.
signatures.failure_boundary: Planner timeouts; the back-translation step and execution on a robot are not evaluated.

gap.author_gap: LLMs are fluent but cannot reliably produce correct or optimal long-horizon plans; classical planners are sound and complete but need formal input.
gap.checked_gap: Real and supported within the paper: LLM-as-P (with or without an example) is feasible on only about 17% of tasks and optimal on about 9% (our computation from Table I) and ToT times out. The closest competitors (prompting/fine-tuning for PDDL, concurrent [66]) are cited by number only and not compared.
lineage: LLM planners (Huang et al., SayCan, Vemprala et al.) -> LLM + external tools (calculators, ToolFormer) -> concurrent LLM+PDDL on the SayCan dataset [66] -> LLM+P (problem translation + off-the-shelf optimal planner)
gap.closest_adjacent: Concurrent LLM+PDDL work [66] and prompting/fine-tuning works [47-57] are named without results; direct comparison is only against LLM-as-P and Tree-of-Thoughts.
gap.residue: Getting verifiably optimal long-horizon plans from natural-language task descriptions without the LLM doing the search.
gap.stakes: Plan optimality and feasibility on combinatorial robot task domains (plan cost 22 vs 31 in the demo).
gap.method_response: Restrict the LLM to translation into PDDL with a one-shot example and hand the search to a sound planner.
gap.remaining_gap: Human-written domain PDDL and example, translation errors undetected (no repair loop), routing between LLM+P and plain chat left to future work, three domains below 25% optimal, and no closed-loop robot execution evidence.
gap.current_relevance: Not assessed from later work; no later paper in the pinned local set bears on it.
unresolved: Neighbour methods are cited without results, so the lineage position is taken from the paper's text only.

claims.result_denominator: LLM+P optimal-alias successes 64/140 (45.7%); feasible incl. lama fallback 97/140 (69.3%); LLM-as-P with context optimal 13/140 (9.3%), correct 24/140 (17.1%); one deterministic response per task

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Quantitative results are open-loop symbolic plan outcomes; the robot demonstration is one qualitative scenario without trial counts.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: LLM+P turns a natural-language planning problem into a PDDL problem file with a GPT-4 one-shot prompt, solves it with a classical planner (Fast Downward), and translates the plan back to natural language; LLM+P is able to provide optimal solutions for most problems while LLMs on their own fail to provide even feasible plans for most problems, and it is demonstrated on a real-robot tidy-up task.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Given an expert-written domain file and one worked example per domain, GPT-4 translation plus Fast Downward returns feasible plans for 97/140 and confirmed-optimal plans for 64/140 generated tasks across seven IPC robot-planning domains (Floortile 0%), versus about 17% correct for direct GPT-4 planning; the example is indispensable. 'Optimal for most problems' and closed-loop robot performance are not shown.

G.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Clear, important gap (LLM long-horizon planning unreliable; sound solvers need formal input) with the baseline failure measured on the same benchmark; neighbours ([47-57], concurrent [66]) cited without results.

M.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Translation-not-planning is a well-fitted seam; the solver guarantees correctness conditional on the problem file; context/no-context gives a distinguishable prediction. Translation correctness is unchecked and the expert domain file carries much of the burden.

X.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Pipeline, model, temperature, planner aliases, time limit and assumptions are stated. Not 4: provenance of NL descriptions, full prompts and robot execution interface absent; no retry flow.

measurement.reason: Both 2; confirmed, with an added validator note. One deterministic response per task, 20 tasks per domain, hand-counted baselines, one qualitative robot scenario; in addition the text never states that LLM+P plans were validated against the ground-truth problem PDDL, so a mistranslated but solvable problem could be counted as success (validator gap).

causality.reason: Both 2; confirmed. Same-GPT-4 comparisons (direct, with/without example, ToT) and a no-context ablation, but only LLM+P receives the expert domain file, so solver delegation is not separated from added formal knowledge; single backbone.

holdout.reason: Both 2; confirmed. One example per domain, generated instances, no described tuning; public IPC domains with unexamined pretraining exposure; robot demo a single case.

statistics.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Single deterministic run per task, no variance/CI, translation failures described not counted.

cost.reason: Resolved toward sol (son55 1). The call budget is inferable from the design (one translation and one back-translation call, temperature 0) and the 200 s search cap is shared by the planner and ToT; the human-written domain file is an extra information channel given only to LLM+P and left unpriced; no times/tokens. This is the anchor-2 instance (call budget inferable, extra channel unpriced).

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE excludes general LLM work that only mentions robots in passing. LLM+P makes robot task planning its explicit application (agg:E002), evaluates on seven IPC robot-planning domains, poses a service-robot question (agg:E003) and executes a plan on a real robot; its LLM-to-PDDL-to-solver loop is the canonical instance of the in-domain R01 harness pattern. The method is general (agg:E004), but the right place to record the missing closed-loop embodiment is evidence_level=offline and the E ratings, not exclusion (exclusion would turn an evidence weakness into a scope verdict). Anchor precedent 2 (no frontier LLM / human teacher) does not apply.

resolutions.final_value: scoped; sub-claim 'optimal for most problems' unsupported by Table I (64/140 confirmed optimal); 'correct for most' supported (97/140) conditional on an expert domain file and one example
resolutions.reason: Table I semantics fixed by V-B (agg:E001). Lama-fallback plans may sometimes be optimal, but the paper does not verify this, so 'optimal for most' is unsupported rather than proven false; the feasible-plan majority holds. Per-domain majority-optimal holds in 3 of 7 domains.

C25 is the only child of decompose_and_delegate and names exactly this move (a formal domain/world model emitted by the LLM and routed to a classical planner); LLM+P executes steps 1-2 fully and lacks step 3 (no solver-feedback repair) and step 5 (cost): a partial tactical match recorded with missing steps, not 'no applicable sub-card' (consistent with ProgPrompt/DEPS in this batch). Supporting adapt_via_conditioning adopted from son55 because the one-shot (NL, PDDL) context is a separately ablated, load-bearing operation (0% in every domain without it); its sub is null because C03 requires an upstream schema-parsing phase or a reference substrate, and LLM+P has one hand-written example per domain.
Anchor-2 instance: inferable call budget, shared search cap, unpriced extra knowledge channel.
Single deterministic run; no repeats, CIs or paired tests.
No planning time, calls, tokens or USD; the cap is credited under E.cost.
No statement on development overlap or on GPT-4 exposure to the public IPC domains/generators.
